newsitem.title: USA: Milken probation extended six more months - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Milken probation extended six more months - NYT.

text.p: Michael Milken has agreed to extend his probation another six months to give the government time to finish investigating whether he honoured terms of an agreement which barred him from the securities industry for life, the New York Times said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said an existing extension of Milken's probation was set to expire on April 25 but lawyers were still reviewing evidence related to his business activities.
The SEC has been investigating Milken's role in several transactions, including MCI Communications's agreement to invest as much as $2 billion in News Corp.
Milken, who pioneered the use of junk bonds, pleaded guilty to six counts of securities fraud in 1990, served two years in prison, and paid more than $1 billion in fines and restitution.
